title: Cayley-Hamilton minpoly OQ05/OQ01/OQ04: cyclic vectors over arbitrary fields

problemStatement.formal: \text{If }M\in M_n(K)\text{ is nonderogatory, then }\exists v:K^n\text{ such that }v\text{ is cyclic for }M\text{ over every field }K.
problemStatement.plain: Every nonderogatory matrix over any field has a cyclic vector, including finite fields where the usual union-avoidance proof fails.
whyMatters: Removes the infinite-field/cardinality restriction from the cyclic-vector theorem.

# Knowledge Base: Cayley-Hamilton minpoly OQ05/OQ01/OQ04

## Verified State

The child proof closes the all-fields nonderogatory-to-cyclic-vector theorem in `Proofs/CayleyHamiltonMinpolyOQ05OQ01OQ04.lean`. The manifest reports 287 lines, 7 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 axioms, and 0 sorries.

## Key Result

`nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_any_field` proves that every nonderogatory matrix has a cyclic vector over any field. The proof delegates to the WIP05 UFD factorization wrapper and WIP04 Bezout/CRT primary-decomposition argument, so no PID structure theorem is assumed.

## Notes

`F2_union_covers` records why the usual union-avoidance proof breaks over small finite fields. That example is a limitation of the counting argument only; the algebraic theorem remains true over finite and infinite fields.
